How to read this report
  • A run's score is the weighted fraction of its graders that passed; a "perfect" run passed every grader.
  • A case's score is the mean of its runs; a case passes when its score is at or above the 100% threshold (the tick on each case bar).
  • The suite score is the mean of the per-case scores.
  • Judge votes are independent samples of the LLM judge; the majority decides pass or fail.
  • "With plugin" and "Baseline" runs are identical except for the plugin being loaded; Δ is the with-plugin score minus the baseline score.

✓ pass 01-recall-imvigor210

judge votes: PASS PASS PASS

Judge votes✓ ✓ ✓
Evidence (what the judge was shown; for an image, a description of what was sent)
I found 12 cohorts you can download today with no application, covering melanoma, gastric, lung, urothelial and glioblastoma, so you can validate across studies straight away. The most valuable data for melanoma, kidney and large lung trials is under controlled access, but the processed melanoma and kidney matrices are published in the papers' supplements.

I checked everything on 2026-11-12. NCBI's GEO and dbGaP web pages blocked automated access, so I confirmed the GEO studies through NCBI's FTP server, which listed each study's files and title. Response labels and sample counts mostly come from my memory of the papers. Check them in each study's sample table or the paper's supplement.

## What I assumed you need
- **R1 (must):** patients treated with anti-PD-1/PD-L1 and/or anti-CTLA-4.
- **R2 (must):** bulk tumour RNA-seq taken before treatment.
- **R3 (must):** a response label for each patient (RECIST or clinical benefit).
- **R4 (must):** several independent cohorts.
- **R5 (nice to have):** downloadable today.

## Shortlist
| # | Cohort | Cancer / drug | Access | Size (from memory) | Checked |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **IMvigor210CoreBiologies** (Mariathasan 2018) | Urothelial, atezolizumab | **Open**: R package tarball | ~348 patients, ~298 with RECIST | today (download link) |
| 2 | **Riaz 2017**, GSE91061 | Melanoma, nivolumab (with or without prior ipilimumab) | **Open**: raw counts and FPKM on GEO | 51 before / 58 during treatment, 65 patients | today (BioProject page) |
| 3 | **Gide 2019**, PRJEB23709 | Melanoma, anti-PD-1 or ipilimumab + nivolumab | **Open**: raw reads on ENA | ~90 samples | today (ENA's API) |
| 4 | **Kim 2018**, PRJEB25780 | Gastric, pembrolizumab | **Open**: raw reads on ENA | ~45 with RNA-seq, 61 patients | today (ENA's API) |
| 5 | **Hugo 2016**, GSE78220 | Melanoma, anti-PD-1 | **Open**: FPKM spreadsheet on GEO | ~28 | today |
| 6 | **Jung 2019**, GSE135222 | Lung (NSCLC), anti-PD-1/PD-L1 | **Open**: expression table on GEO | ~27; benefit defined by PFS | today |
| 7 | **Auslander 2018**, GSE115821 | Melanoma, anti-PD-1/CTLA-4 | **Open**: counts on GEO | ~37 samples, some during treatment | today |
| 8 | **Rose 2021**, GSE176307 | Urothelial, real-world ICI | **Open**: normalised data and RSEM files on GEO | response field not checked | today |
| 9 | **Snyder 2017**, Zenodo 546110 | Urothelial, atezolizumab | **Open**, CC BY 4.0, kallisto quantifications | ~25 | today (Zenodo's API) |
| 10 | **Cho 2020**, GSE126044 | Lung (NSCLC), anti-PD-1 | **Open**: counts on GEO | ~16 | today |
| 11 | Zhao 2019, PRJNA482620 | Glioblastoma, anti-PD-1 | **Open**: raw reads on SRA (open status from memory) | small; response is not RECIST | today (page exists) |
| 12 | Cloughesy 2019, GSE121810 | Glioblastoma, neoadjuvant pembrolizumab | **Open** | small; outcome is survival, not response | today |
| 13 | **Liu 2019 + Van Allen 2015**, dbGaP phs000452 | Melanoma, anti-PD-1 / ipilimumab | Raw data: **dbGaP application, weeks**. Processed TPM + clinical table: **open in the Nat Med supplement** (from memory) | ~120 (Liu) + ~40 (Van Allen) | page exists; terms from memory |
| 14 | **Braun 2020** (CheckMate 009/010/025), Miao 2018 | Kidney (RCC), nivolumab | Raw data: **dbGaP application** (page says "Request access via Authorized Access", "Data Use Certification Agreement"). Processed data: open in the supplement (from memory) | ~180 | today (dbGaP page read) |
| 15 | **OAK/POPLAR** (Patil 2022), EGAS00001005013 | NSCLC, atezolizumab vs docetaxel | **Data Access Committee (DAC) application, months** | ~900, randomised | today (EGA page) |
| 16 | IMvigor210 raw reads, EGAS00001002556 | Urothelial | **DAC application** | same patients as #1 | today (EGA page) |

## Details that matter
- **IMvigor210:** download `http://research-pub.gene.com/IMvigor210CoreBiologies/IMvigor210CoreBiologies.tar.gz`. It contains counts plus best overall response (`binaryResponse`), mutation burden (TMB) and immune phenotype. The package depends on old Bioconductor versions. If installing it fails, load the `.rda` files directly. I believe the licence is CC BY 3.0 (from memory).
- **Riaz, Hugo, Auslander, Jung, Cho, Rose:** the GEO supplementary files exist (I saw the file listings). For Riaz, the per-patient best overall response is in the paper's supplementary table, not in GEO. Match on patient ID.
- **Gide and Kim:** raw FASTQ only, so plan a day to quantify them with salmon. Run Riaz and Hugo's raw reads (also open on SRA, from memory) through the same pipeline to cut down batch effects.
- **Liu 2019 / Braun 2020:** most published classifiers use the processed matrices from the supplements, so you can use these cohorts now without dbGaP. You only need a dbGaP application (eRA Commons login plus your institution's signing official, typically 2–6 weeks) if you want uniform reprocessing from raw reads.
- **OAK/POPLAR:** this is the strongest validation set because it is large and randomised against docetaxel, which separates "predicts ICI benefit" from "just prognostic". Access goes through an EGA application to the Roche/Genentech access committee, which takes months and isn't guaranteed.
- **Shortcuts:** CRI iAtlas (its site lists 23 ICI datasets; confirmed today), TIGER (tiger.canceromics.org) and TIDE already host harmonised versions of most of the open cohorts. They're useful for cross-checking your labels. I'd still build from the original sources so you control the processing.

## Known, not confirmed
- **JAVELIN Renal 101** (avelumab + axitinib) and **IMmotion150/151** (atezolizumab, RCC): these are on EGA under controlled access, from memory. The EGA accession I tried pointed to an unrelated prostate study, so look up the correct accession in the papers' data statements.
- **Ravi 2023 SU2C-MARK NSCLC** (Nat Genet; 393 patients with WES and/or RNA-seq and response): it came up in the literature search. I didn't check how to get the data.
- **Snyder 2017** may partly overlap with IMvigor210 patients. Check before treating it as an independent cohort.

## Not recommended
- **TCGA:** patients weren't treated with checkpoint inhibitors.
- **MSK-IMPACT / Samstein 2019:** DNA panel only, no RNA.
- **Rizvi 2015 and Le 2015:** exome sequencing only.
- **Prat 2017:** NanoString panel, not RNA-seq.
- **Zenodo "Immunotherapy Clonal Dynamics Cohort":** a commercial vendor's free sample with unclear provenance.

## Next step
A practical split:
- **Training:** Liu 2019 (supplement) + Riaz + Gide + Hugo, all melanoma.
- **Validation in other cancers:** IMvigor210, Kim gastric, Braun RCC (supplement), and Jung/Cho NSCLC.
- **Application to start now:** OAK/POPLAR, for the randomised predictive-vs-prognostic test.

I didn't check the per-sample response fields for Rose (GSE176307) and Cho (GSE126044), so look at those first.

The interactive shortlist is at `/private/tmp/e-uFqWsj/home/cwd/dataset-shortlist.html`. The working files, including the list of everything checked, are in `dataset-scout/`.

## Details that matter
- **IMvigor210:** download `http://research-pub.gene.com/IMvigor210CoreBiologies/IMvigor210CoreBiologies.tar.gz`. It contains counts plus best overall response (`binaryResponse`), mutation burden (TMB) and immune phenotype. The package depends on old Bioconductor versions. If installing it fails, load the `.rda` files directly. I believe the licence is CC BY 3.0 (from memory).
- **Riaz, Hugo, Auslander, Jung, Cho, Rose:** the GEO supplementary files exist (I saw the file listings). For Riaz, the per-patient best overall response is in the paper's supplementary table, not in GEO. Match on patient ID.
- **Gide and Kim:** raw FASTQ only, so plan a day to quantify them with salmon. Run Riaz and Hugo's raw reads (also open on SRA, from memory) through the same pipeline to cut down batch effects.
- **Liu 2019 / Braun 2020:** most published classifiers use the processed matrices from the supplements, so you can use these cohorts now without dbGaP. You only need a dbGaP application (eRA Commons login plus your institution's signing official, typically 2–6 weeks) if you want uniform reprocessing from raw reads.
- **OAK/POPLAR:** this is the strongest validation set because it is large and randomised against docetaxel, which separates "predicts ICI benefit" from "just prognostic". Access goes through an EGA application to the Roche/Genentech access committee, which takes months and isn't guaranteed.
- **Shortcuts:** CRI iAtlas (its site lists 23 ICI datasets; confirmed today), TIGER (tiger.canceromics.org) and TIDE already host harmonised versions of most of the open cohorts. They're useful for cross-checking your labels. I'd still build from the original sources so you control the processing.

## Known, not confirmed
- **JAVELIN Renal 101** (avelumab + axitinib) and **IMmotion150/151** (atezolizumab, RCC): these are on EGA under controlled access, from memory. The EGA accession I tried pointed to an unrelated prostate study, so look up the correct accession in the papers' data statements.
- **Ravi 2023 SU2C-MARK NSCLC** (Nat Genet; 393 patients with WES and/or RNA-seq and response): it came up in the literature search. I didn't check how to get the data.
- **Snyder 2017** may partly overlap with IMvigor210 patients. Check before treating it as an independent cohort.

## Not recommended
- **TCGA:** patients weren't treated with checkpoint inhibitors.
- **MSK-IMPACT / Samstein 2019:** DNA panel only, no RNA.
- **Rizvi 2015 and Le 2015:** exome sequencing only.
- **Prat 2017:** NanoString panel, not RNA-seq.
- **Zenodo "Immunotherapy Clonal Dynamics Cohort":** a commercial vendor's free sample with unclear provenance.

## Next step
A practical split:
- **Training:** Liu 2019 (supplement) + Riaz + Gide + Hugo, all melanoma.
- **Validation in other cancers:** IMvigor210, Kim gastric, Braun RCC (supplement), and Jung/Cho NSCLC.
- **Application to start now:** OAK/POPLAR, for the randomised predictive-vs-prognostic test.

I didn't check the per-sample response fields for Rose (GSE176307) and Cho (GSE126044), so look at those first.

## What I assumed you need
- **R1 (must):** patients actually treated with anti-PD-1/PD-L1 or anti-CTLA-4, with tumour samples taken **before** treatment
- **R2 (must):** bulk tumour **RNA-seq**. I counted NanoString panels, microarrays and blood samples as not meeting this.
- **R3 (must):** a response label for each patient: RECIST, or clinical benefit
- **R4 (nice to have):** downloadable today. Controlled cohorts are included but ranked lower.

I checked everything on 2026-11-12. GEO and ENA block scripts on their web pages, so I confirmed records through their APIs instead (NCBI E-utilities, ENA portal API, EGA metadata API, cBioPortal API).

## Key finding
**cBioPortal hosts iAtlas-harmonised copies of several major ICI cohorts.** Each has a TPM matrix plus `RESPONSE` and `CLINICAL_BENEFIT` columns, and you can download them now without logging in. This includes cohorts whose raw reads are controlled (Liu 2019 is in dbGaP; IMmotion150 is in EGA). For a classifier you mostly don't need the raw reads, so most of what you need is available today.

## Shortlist
| # | Cohort | Cancer / drug | Pre-treatment RNA-seq n | Access | Checked |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **IMvigor210** (Mariathasan 2018) | Urothelial, atezolizumab | 348 | **Open now:** R package with counts and response; also on cBioPortal. Raw reads: EGA, controlled | today |
| 2 | **Liu 2019** | Melanoma, anti-PD-1 | ~120 | **Open now:** cBioPortal `mel_iatlas_liu_2019`. Raw: dbGaP phs000452 | today |
| 3 | **Gide 2019** | Melanoma, anti-PD-1 ± anti-CTLA-4 | ~70 | **Open now:** raw FASTQ at ENA PRJEB23709; processed copy on cBioPortal | today |
| 4 | **Riaz 2017** GSE91061 | Melanoma, nivolumab | ~51 pre (109 samples) | **Open now:** GEO; labels on cBioPortal | today |
| 5 | **Kim 2018** PRJEB25780 | Gastric, pembrolizumab | ~45 | **Open now:** ENA, raw reads only, so you quantify them yourself | today |
| 6 | **IMmotion150** | Renal cell, atezolizumab ± bevacizumab vs sunitinib | 263 samples | **Open now:** cBioPortal `rcc_iatlas_immotion150_2018`. Raw: EGA | today |
| 7 | **Hugo 2016** GSE78220 | Melanoma, anti-PD-1 | 28 | **Open now:** GEO | today |
| 8 | **Rose 2021** GSE176307 | Urothelial, mixed PD-(L)1 drugs | 89 | **Open now:** GEO | today |
| 9 | **Braun 2020** CheckMate 009/010/025 | Renal cell, nivolumab vs everolimus | ~181 on nivolumab | Paper supplementary tables; raw reads controlled | partly today |
| 10 | **SU2C-MARK** (Ravi 2023) | NSCLC, anti-PD-(L)1 | 152 | Processed data reportedly in the supplement; raw at dbGaP phs002822 | partly today |
| 11 | **POPLAR + OAK** | NSCLC, atezolizumab vs docetaxel | 891 | **Apply:** EGA access committee (Genentech), likely months | today |
| 12 | **Van Allen 2015** | Melanoma, **ipilimumab** (anti-CTLA-4) | 42 | **Apply:** dbGaP phs000452 | from memory |

**Small open GEO/ENA cohorts, useful only for validation:**
- GSE121810 and PRJNA482620: glioblastoma
- GSE135222, GSE136961, GSE126044: NSCLC, n=16–27
- GSE115821: melanoma, mixed timepoints
- GSE181815: thymic carcinoma
- GSE165252: oesophageal, atezolizumab plus chemoradiation, so the treatment is confounded
- GSE168204: mostly on-treatment samples

## Details that matter
- **IMvigor210:** download `IMvigor210CoreBiologies_1.0.1.tar.gz` (74 MB) from research-pub.gene.com/IMvigor210CoreBiologies/packageVersions/. It's the largest open cohort and the usual anchor for training.
  - The RNA was profiled from FFPE tissue with an exome-capture protocol, which differs from the fresh-frozen poly-A RNA-seq in the melanoma cohorts. Expect a platform effect.
  - About a quarter of patients have no evaluable response.
  - I didn't read the package licence.
- **Riaz:** the GEO series doesn't include response labels. Take them from the paper's Table S2 or the cBioPortal copy. Also split ipilimumab-naive from ipilimumab-progressed patients.
- **Gide:** mixes anti-PD-1 alone with the combination. Use treatment as a covariate and drop the on-treatment samples.
- **Liu 2019:** some patients had already received ipilimumab. The cBioPortal `mel_dfci_2019` copy has TPM but no response field, so use the iAtlas copy for labels.
- **Control arms:** Braun (everolimus), IMmotion150 (sunitinib) and POPLAR/OAK (docetaxel) include patients who didn't get a checkpoint inhibitor. They let you show the classifier predicts ICI response specifically, rather than just general prognosis. Reviewers will ask about this.
- **Response definitions differ** between studies: CR/PR versus clinical benefit, which can include stable disease beyond 6 months. Harmonise them before training.
- **Mind the dbGaP/EGA agreements.** If you do get raw controlled data, they generally forbid sending records to third-party online services, which can include hosted AI tools.
- **Usage evidence:** the 2026 Nature Medicine COMPASS paper (doi:10.1038/s41591-026-04502-7) used IMvigor210 from this package and from iAtlas. A 2022 systematic review (PMC9153191) catalogues about 25 ICI transcriptomic cohorts.

## Known, not confirmed
- **TIDE** (tide.dfci.harvard.edu), **TIGER**, **ORCESTRA/PredictIO** and **ICBatlas** are aggregator portals with harmonised ICI cohorts. None of them could be read by script today: they refused automated requests, are JavaScript-only, or returned a 502 error. Open them in a browser.
- The SU2C-MARK and Braun supplementary matrices were reported by papers that reused them; I didn't open the files.
- Van Allen's access details are from memory.

## Not recommended
- GSE100797: adoptive T-cell therapy, not a checkpoint inhibitor
- GSE93157 and GSE165745: NanoString panels
- GSE94873: whole-blood RT-PCR, not tumour
- GSE67501, GSE111636, GSE122220, GSE140901: arrays with n of 24 or fewer
- TCGA: patients weren't treated with checkpoint inhibitors

## Gaps
Apart from Van Allen 2015, I found no sizeable anti-CTLA-4 *monotherapy* RNA-seq cohort. The PD-1 cohorts heavily outweigh CTLA-4 ones.

## Next step
1. **Today:** pull IMvigor210, the cBioPortal iAtlas studies (Liu, Gide, Riaz, IMmotion150), and Hugo and Rose from GEO.
2. Validate with leave-one-cohort-out.
3. Start the POPLAR/OAK EGA application now, since it takes months.

The interactive shortlist (26 entries, filterable, exportable access plan) is at `/private/tmp/e-MGNaSd/home/cwd/dataset-shortlist.html`.

## Key finding

| 5 | **Kim 2018** PRJEB25780 | Gastric, pembrolizumab | ~45 | **Open now:** ENA, raw reads only, so you quantify them yourself | today |
| 6 | **IMmotion150** | Renal cell, atezolizumab ± bevacizumab vs sunitinib | 263 samples | **Open now:** cBioPortal `rcc_iatlas_immotion150_2018`. Raw: EGA | today |

## Details that matter
- **IMvigor210:** download `IMvigor210CoreBiologies_1.0.1.tar.gz` (74 MB) from research-pub.gene.com/IMvigor210CoreBiologies/packageVersions/. It's the largest open cohort and the usual anchor for training.
  - The RNA was profiled from FFPE tissue with an exome-capture protocol, which differs from the fresh-frozen poly-A RNA-seq in the melanoma cohorts. Expect a platform effect.
  - About a quarter of patients have no evaluable response.
  - I didn't read the package licence.
- **Riaz:** the GEO series doesn't include response labels. Take them from the paper's Table S2 or the cBioPortal copy. Also split ipilimumab-naive from ipilimumab-progressed patients.
- **Gide:** mixes anti-PD-1 alone with the combination. Use treatment as a covariate and drop the on-treatment samples.
- **Liu 2019:** some patients had already received ipilimumab. The cBioPortal `mel_dfci_2019` copy has TPM but no response field, so use the iAtlas copy for labels.
- **Control arms:** Braun (everolimus), IMmotion150 (sunitinib) and POPLAR/OAK (docetaxel) include patients who didn't get a checkpoint inhibitor. They let you show the classifier predicts ICI response specifically, rather than just general prognosis. Reviewers will ask about this.
- **Response definitions differ** between studies: CR/PR versus clinical benefit, which can include stable disease beyond 6 months. Harmonise them before training.
- **Mind the dbGaP/EGA agreements.** If you do get raw controlled data, they generally forbid sending records to third-party online services, which can include hosted AI tools.
- **Usage evidence:** the 2026 Nature Medicine COMPASS paper (doi:10.1038/s41591-026-04502-7) used IMvigor210 from this package and from iAtlas. A 2022 systematic review (PMC9153191) catalogues about 25 ICI transcriptomic cohorts.

## Known, not confirmed
- **TIDE** (tide.dfci.harvard.edu), **TIGER**, **ORCESTRA/PredictIO** and **ICBatlas** are aggregator portals with harmonised ICI cohorts. None of them could be read by script today: they refused automated requests, are JavaScript-only, or returned a 502 error. Open them in a browser.
- The SU2C-MARK and Braun supplementary matrices were reported by papers that reused them; I didn't open the files.
- Van Allen's access details are from memory.

## Not recommended
- GSE100797: adoptive T-cell therapy, not a checkpoint inhibitor
- GSE93157 and GSE165745: NanoString panels
- GSE94873: whole-blood RT-PCR, not tumour
- GSE67501, GSE111636, GSE122220, GSE140901: arrays with n of 24 or fewer
- TCGA: patients weren't treated with checkpoint inhibitors

## Gaps
Apart from Van Allen 2015, I found no sizeable anti-CTLA-4 *monotherapy* RNA-seq cohort. The PD-1 cohorts heavily outweigh CTLA-4 ones.

## Next step
1. **Today:** pull IMvigor210, the cBioPortal iAtlas studies (Liu, Gide, Riaz, IMmotion150), and Hugo and Rose from GEO.
2. Validate with leave-one-cohort-out.
3. Start the POPLAR/OAK EGA application now, since it takes months.

## What I assumed you need
- **R1 (must):** patients actually treated with anti-PD-1/PD-L1 or anti-CTLA-4, with tumour samples taken **before** treatment
- **R2 (must):** bulk tumour **RNA-seq**. I counted NanoString panels, microarrays and blood samples as not meeting this.
- **R3 (must):** a response label for each patient: RECIST, or clinical benefit
- **R4 (nice to have):** downloadable today. Controlled cohorts are included but ranked lower.

I checked everything on 2026-11-12. GEO and ENA block scripts on their web pages, so I confirmed records through their APIs instead (NCBI E-utilities, ENA portal API, EGA metadata API, cBioPortal API).

## Key finding
**cBioPortal hosts iAtlas-harmonised copies of several major ICI cohorts.** Each has a TPM matrix plus `RESPONSE` and `CLINICAL_BENEFIT` columns, and you can download them now without logging in. This includes cohorts whose raw reads are controlled (Liu 2019 is in dbGaP; IMmotion150 is in EGA). For a classifier you mostly don't need the raw reads, so most of what you need is available today.

## Shortlist

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **IMvigor210** (Mariathasan 2018) | Urothelial, atezolizumab | 348 | **Open now:** R package with counts and response; also on cBioPortal. Raw reads: EGA, controlled | today |
| 2 | **Liu 2019** | Melanoma, anti-PD-1 | ~120 | **Open now:** cBioPortal `mel_iatlas_liu_2019`. Raw: dbGaP phs000452 | today |
| 3 | **Gide 2019** | Melanoma, anti-PD-1 ± anti-CTLA-4 | ~70 | **Open now:** raw FASTQ at ENA PRJEB23709; processed copy on cBioPortal | today |

| 5 | **Kim 2018** PRJEB25780 | Gastric, pembrolizumab | ~45 | **Open now:** ENA, raw reads only, so you quantify them yourself | today |
| 6 | **IMmotion150** | Renal cell, atezolizumab ± bevacizumab vs sunitinib | 263 samples | **Open now:** cBioPortal `rcc_iatlas_immotion150_2018`. Raw: EGA | today |
| 7 | **Hugo 2016** GSE78220 | Melanoma, anti-PD-1 | 28 | **Open now:** GEO | today |
| 8 | **Rose 2021** GSE176307 | Urothelial, mixed PD-(L)1 drugs | 89 | **Open now:** GEO | today |

- GSE168204: mostly on-treatment samples

## Details that matter
- **IMvigor210:** download `IMvigor210CoreBiologies_1.0.1.tar.gz` (74 MB) from research-pub.gene.com/IMvigor210CoreBiologies/packageVersions/. It's the largest open cohort and the usual anchor for training.
  - The RNA was profiled from FFPE tissue with an exome-capture protocol, which differs from the fresh-frozen poly-A RNA-seq in the melanoma cohorts. Expect a platform effect.
  - About a quarter of patients have no evaluable response.
  - I didn't read the package licence.
- **Riaz:** the GEO series doesn't include response labels. Take them from the paper's Table S2 or the cBioPortal copy. Also split ipilimumab-naive from ipilimumab-progressed patients.
- **Gide:** mixes anti-PD-1 alone with the combination. Use treatment as a covariate and drop the on-treatment samples.
- **Liu 2019:** some patients had already received ipilimumab. The cBioPortal `mel_dfci_2019` copy has TPM but no response field, so use the iAtlas copy for labels.
- **Control arms:** Braun (everolimus), IMmotion150 (sunitinib) and POPLAR/OAK (docetaxel) include patients who didn't get a checkpoint inhibitor. They let you show the classifier predicts ICI response specifically, rather than just general prognosis. Reviewers will ask about this.
- **Response definitions differ** between studies: CR/PR versus clinical benefit, which can include stable disease beyond 6 months. Harmonise them before training.
- **Mind the dbGaP/EGA agreements.** If you do get raw controlled data, they generally forbid sending records to third-party online services, which can include hosted AI tools.
- **Usage evidence:** the 2026 Nature Medicine COMPASS paper (doi:10.1038/s41591-026-04502-7) used IMvigor210 from this package and from iAtlas. A 2022 systematic review (PMC9153191) catalogues about 25 ICI transcriptomic cohorts.

- The SU2C-MARK and Braun supplementary matrices were reported by papers that reused them; I didn't open the files.
- Van Allen's access details are from memory.

## Not recommended
- GSE100797: adoptive T-cell therapy, not a checkpoint inhibitor
- GSE93157 and GSE165745: NanoString panels
- GSE94873: whole-blood RT-PCR, not tumour
- GSE67501, GSE111636, GSE122220, GSE140901: arrays with n of 24 or fewer
- TCGA: patients weren't treated with checkpoint inhibitors

There are about 12 cohorts you can download today, across melanoma, urothelial, kidney, gastric, glioblastoma and lung cancer. That is enough for leave-one-study-out validation. Most of the very large trial cohorts need an application, and lung cancer is where that hurts most.

I checked every link and accession today (2026-11-12). Anything marked "from memory" is something I couldn't confirm today. GEO's web pages blocked automated access, so I confirmed the GEO series through NCBI's programmatic API instead (title and sample count for each).

## What I assumed you need
- **R1 (must):** patients actually treated with anti-PD-1, anti-PD-L1 or anti-CTLA-4
- **R2 (must):** bulk tumour RNA-seq, before treatment
- **R3 (must):** a response label for each patient (RECIST or clinical benefit)
- **R4 (preferred):** downloadable now; if not, the application route stated
- I assumed microarray and NanoString data don't count, and that trials combining a checkpoint inhibitor with other drugs count for less.

## Shortlist

**Download today**

| # | Cohort | Cancer / drug | Data | Access | Checked |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Riaz 2017**, GSE91061 | Melanoma, nivolumab | 109 samples, before and during treatment | Open | today |
| 2 | **Gide 2019**, ENA PRJEB23709 | Melanoma, anti-PD-1 with or without ipilimumab | 91 runs, raw FASTQ only | Open | today |
| 3 | **IMvigor210CoreBiologies** (R package) | Urothelial, atezolizumab | 368 patients, processed counts plus clinical data | Open | today |
| 4 | **Braun 2020**, CheckMate 009/010/025 | Kidney (clear cell), nivolumab vs everolimus | Normalised RNA-seq in Supplementary Table 4 | Open (journal supplement) | today |
| 5 | **Rose 2021**, GSE176307 | Urothelial, anti-PD-1/PD-L1 | 90 samples | Open | today |
| 6 | **Hugo 2016**, GSE78220 | Melanoma, anti-PD-1 | 28 samples, before treatment | Open | today |
| 7 | **Kim 2018**, ENA PRJEB25780 | Gastric, pembrolizumab | 188 runs, including whole-exome; about 45 RNA-seq patients (from memory) | Open, raw only | today |
| 8 | **Cloughesy 2019**, GSE121810 | Glioblastoma, pembrolizumab before surgery | 29 samples; outcome is survival | Open | today |
| 9 | **Auslander 2018**, GSE115821 | Melanoma, anti-PD-1/anti-CTLA-4 | 37 samples, mixed timepoints | Open | today |
| 10 | **Jung 2019**, GSE135222 | Lung (NSCLC), anti-PD-(L)1 | 27 samples; benefit defined by PFS | Open | today |
| 11 | **Hwang 2020**, GSE136961 | Lung (NSCLC), anti-PD-1 | 21 samples; durable clinical benefit | Open | today |

**Application needed**

| # | Cohort | Cancer / drug | Data | Access | Checked |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| 14 | **Liu 2019 / Van Allen 2015**, dbGaP phs000452 | Melanoma, anti-PD-1 (about 120) and ipilimumab (about 40) | RNA-seq | Raw reads via dbGaP request; processed tables in the paper supplements (from memory) | today |
| 15 | IMvigor210 raw reads, EGA EGAS00001002556 | Urothelial, atezolizumab | Raw FASTQ | EGA access committee (Genentech), months | today |
| 16 | IMmotion150 (McDermott 2018) | Kidney, atezolizumab with or without bevacizumab | RNA-seq | EGA access committee | from memory |
| 17 | OAK/POPLAR (Patil 2022) | Lung (NSCLC), atezolizumab vs docetaxel | RNA-seq | EGA, Genentech committee | from memory |
| 18 | JAVELIN Renal 101 (Motzer 2020) | Kidney, avelumab plus axitinib | RNA-seq | Request to Pfizer | from memory |

## Details that matter for your design
- **Response labels usually aren't in GEO or ENA.** For Riaz, Gide, Kim, Hugo and Rose they are in the papers' supplementary clinical tables. IMvigor210 is the exception: best overall response is in the package's sample annotation (from memory).
- **Platform effects:** IMvigor210 used a capture-based library method (TruSeq RNA Access), not the usual poly-A method. Gide and Kim give you raw FASTQ only. Reprocessing everything with one pipeline (for example salmon) will help cross-study transfer.
- **Only keep pre-treatment samples.** Riaz, Auslander and Cloughesy mix in samples taken during treatment, or after treatment before surgery.
- **Possible patient overlap:** GSE135222 and GSE136961 are both Korean lung cancer cohorts, so check for shared patients before using one to validate the other.
- **Liu 2019:** the paper says "Raw sequencing data are available in dbGaP (accession number phs000452.v3.p1)." Its processed expression table in the supplement (from memory) means you can start before any approval.
- **SU2C-MARK:** use limits vary by contributing hospital (some disease-specific only, some general research). Samples from Cleveland Clinic and UC Davis were not deposited.
- **Braun 2020:** the paper says "Normalized RNA-seq expression data … are available in Supplementary Table 4." There are no raw RNA-seq reads. Exome data are at EGA (EGAS00001004290 to EGAS00001004292) under controlled access.
- **Licences:** I couldn't confirm the IMvigor210 package licence today (CC BY 3.0 from memory; check the package's DESCRIPTION file). Journal supplements fall under the publisher's reuse terms.
- **Benchmark papers worth reading:** two comparisons of published expression-based response markers (Cancers 2021, doi:10.3390/cancers13071639, and Cancers 2023, doi:10.3390/cancers15164094, which curated 29 cohorts with about 1,400 patients). There is also a meta-analysis of six bladder cancer cohorts (Nat Commun 2025, doi:10.1038/s41467-025-56462-0). Their cohort tables are a good way to find what I missed.

## Not recommended, and why
- **GSE93157 and GSE173839:** NanoString panel and microarray, not RNA-seq. GSE173839 also combines the checkpoint inhibitor with a PARP inhibitor and chemotherapy.
- **GSE165252 (PERFECT trial):** atezolizumab was given with chemoradiotherapy, so response can't be credited to the checkpoint inhibitor.
- **GSE100797 (Lauss 2017):** adoptive T-cell therapy, not checkpoint inhibitors (from memory).
- **Compendia (CPI1000+, TIGER, CRI iAtlas, TIDE):** these re-process the same cohorts listed above. They are handy for harmonised matrices but are not independent cohorts, so don't count them as extra validation sets.

## What I couldn't find
- An open, large lung cancer cohort. The big ones (SU2C-MARK, OAK/POPLAR) all need applications.
- Many anti-CTLA-4-only RNA-seq cohorts beyond Van Allen 2015.
- I couldn't confirm the access terms for IMmotion150, OAK/POPLAR or JAVELIN today.

## Next step
1. Download cohorts 1–8 and 10–12, plus the Liu and Van Allen supplement tables.
2. Reprocess the raw-only sets (Gide, Kim) with the same pipeline as the rest.
3. File the dbGaP request for SU2C-MARK now, since it takes weeks, and use it as a held-out lung cancer test set.

I also built an interactive version of this list, where you can filter the cohorts and export an access plan: `/private/tmp/e-SBuduR/home/cwd/dataset-shortlist.html`

## Details that matter for your design
- **Response labels usually aren't in GEO or ENA.** For Riaz, Gide, Kim, Hugo and Rose they are in the papers' supplementary clinical tables. IMvigor210 is the exception: best overall response is in the package's sample annotation (from memory).
- **Platform effects:** IMvigor210 used a capture-based library method (TruSeq RNA Access), not the usual poly-A method. Gide and Kim give you raw FASTQ only. Reprocessing everything with one pipeline (for example salmon) will help cross-study transfer.
- **Only keep pre-treatment samples.** Riaz, Auslander and Cloughesy mix in samples taken during treatment, or after treatment before surgery.
- **Possible patient overlap:** GSE135222 and GSE136961 are both Korean lung cancer cohorts, so check for shared patients before using one to validate the other.
- **Liu 2019:** the paper says "Raw sequencing data are available in dbGaP (accession number phs000452.v3.p1)." Its processed expression table in the supplement (from memory) means you can start before any approval.
- **SU2C-MARK:** use limits vary by contributing hospital (some disease-specific only, some general research). Samples from Cleveland Clinic and UC Davis were not deposited.

- An open, large lung cancer cohort. The big ones (SU2C-MARK, OAK/POPLAR) all need applications.

Evidence (what the judge was shown; for an image, a description of what was sent)
Several good cohorts are fully open, and a few aggregator resources have already reprocessed most of them. I'm writing this from memory and didn't check the links in this session, so confirm each accession on its landing page before you build a pipeline around it. The ones I'm less sure of are marked "(verify)".

## Download right away (open access)

| Cohort | Cancer / drug | ~Patients with RNA-seq | Where | What you get |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Mariathasan 2018 (IMvigor210)** | Urothelial, atezolizumab (anti-PD-L1) | ~350 | Bioconductor-style R package `IMvigor210CoreBiologies` (from the Genentech/research-pub site) | Processed counts + RECIST + overall survival. Raw data is on EGA (controlled). Biggest single cohort, so a good anchor. |
| **Gide 2019** | Melanoma, anti-PD-1 ± ipilimumab | ~90 samples (pre and some on-treatment) | ENA **PRJEB23709** | Raw FASTQ. Clinical data is in the paper's supplement. |
| **Riaz 2017 (CheckMate 038)** | Melanoma, nivolumab; ipilimumab-naive and ipilimumab-progressed arms | ~50 pre-treatment, plus on-treatment | GEO **GSE91061**; raw on SRA (PRJNA356761) | Counts/FPKM. Response is in the supplement and GitHub (riazn/bms038_analysis). |
| **Hugo 2016** | Melanoma, anti-PD-1 | 28 | GEO **GSE78220** | FPKM; raw on SRA |
| **Kim 2018** | Gastric, pembrolizumab | ~45 | ENA **PRJEB25780** | Raw FASTQ |
| **Rose 2021** | Urothelial, anti-PD-1/PD-L1 | ~90 | GEO **GSE176307** (verify) | Processed expression |
| **Braun 2020 (CheckMate 009/010/025)** | ccRCC, nivolumab vs everolimus | ~180 on the nivolumab arms | Nat Med supplement | Processed expression and clinical data in the supplement; raw is controlled |
| **Small NSCLC cohorts** | NSCLC, anti-PD-1 | 16–30 each | GEO **GSE126044** (Cho), **GSE135222** (Jung), **GSE136961** (Hwang) (verify) | Processed. Small, but they add cancer-type diversity. |
| **Zhao 2019 / Cloughesy 2019** | GBM, anti-PD-1 (incl. neoadjuvant) | ~15–30 | SRA PRJNA482620 / GEO GSE121810 | Response is weak in GBM, so these are better as negative controls than as training data |

## Have to apply (dbGaP / EGA)

- **Van Allen 2015** (melanoma, anti-CTLA-4) and **Liu 2019** (melanoma, anti-PD-1, ~120 with RNA-seq): dbGaP **phs000452**. Both papers' supplements include processed TPM, which is usually enough for a classifier. Apply only if you want uniform reprocessing from raw.
- **Miao 2018** (ccRCC), **Snyder 2017** (urothelial), **Nathanson 2017** (melanoma, anti-CTLA-4): dbGaP. Some processed data is in the supplements or cBioPortal.
- **Atezolizumab NSCLC trials OAK/POPLAR** (Patil 2022, Cancer Cell): EGA, roughly 900 patients. This is the largest NSCLC resource, but access goes through a Roche data access committee.
- **JAVELIN Renal 101** (Motzer 2020, avelumab + axitinib) and **IMmotion150/151** (ccRCC, atezolizumab ± bevacizumab): EGA, controlled.
- **Ravi 2023 SU2C-MARK** (NSCLC, ~150 with RNA-seq): raw data is controlled; check the supplement and GitHub for processed matrices (verify).

dbGaP typically takes 4–8 weeks and needs an institutional signing official. EGA committees vary a lot, and industry-trial data is the slowest.

## Already-harmonised collections (fastest start)

- **CRI iAtlas, ICI module** (iatlas.org; data on Synapse): harmonised expression and response for about a dozen cohorts. It covers many of the ones above, including some controlled cohorts in processed form.
- **TIGER** (tiger.canceromics.org): bulk and single-cell ICI cohorts with response labels.
- **TIDE** (tide.dfci.harvard.edu): processed ICI cohorts used to benchmark TIDE.
- **ICBatlas** and **CAMOIP**: similar portals.
- **Litchfield 2021 (Cell, "CPI1000+")**: a meta-analysis with processed data on Zenodo, covering about 1,000 patients across 12 cohorts (RNA-seq for a subset).

These save a lot of work. Still, I'd re-derive at least the response labels and sample selection from the original papers, because harmonisation choices differ between portals.

## Pitfalls for cross-study validation

1. **Use pre-treatment samples only.** Riaz, Gide and others mix pre- and on-treatment samples in the same series.
2. **Response definitions differ.** Some studies use RECIST CR/PR vs SD/PD. Others use "clinical benefit", which can count SD lasting at least 6 months, and Van Allen and Liu use their own definitions. Pick one rule and reapply it to every cohort where the data allows. Decide explicitly where stable disease goes.
3. **Prior treatment.** Riaz splits patients by prior ipilimumab, and Gide mixes monotherapy with combination therapy. Treat these as covariates or analyse them as separate strata.
4. **Overlapping patients.** Aggregators and meta-analyses can include the same patients under different IDs. Most published response signatures, such as TIDE and IMPRES, were also built or tuned on exactly these cohorts. A truly held-out validation set is harder to find than it looks, so record which cohorts each comparator signature has already seen.
5. **Batch and platform effects.** Studies differ in poly-A vs capture library prep, FFPE vs fresh-frozen tissue, and processing (FPKM vs TPM vs counts). Rank-based or within-sample features hold up better across studies than z-scores across samples. Leave-one-cohort-out validation is the honest test.
6. **Imbalance by cancer type.** Melanoma dominates the open data. IMvigor210 is about 3× bigger than any other single cohort, so weight or stratify for it, or it will drive your model.

## Suggested starting set

Today you can download IMvigor210, Gide, Riaz, Hugo, Kim and Braun, plus the Liu and Van Allen supplementary TPMs. That gives you roughly 750 patients across 4 cancer types, which is enough for leave-one-cohort-out validation with no data access applications. File the dbGaP request for phs000452 and an EGA request for OAK/POPLAR now if you want raw data or a large NSCLC test set later.

I can also write a script that pulls the open cohorts, harmonises gene IDs and response labels, and runs a leave-one-cohort-out setup.

| **Zhao 2019 / Cloughesy 2019** | GBM, anti-PD-1 (incl. neoadjuvant) | ~15–30 | SRA PRJNA482620 / GEO GSE121810 | Response is weak in GBM, so these are better as negative controls than as training data |

## Have to apply (dbGaP / EGA)

- **Van Allen 2015** (melanoma, anti-CTLA-4) and **Liu 2019** (melanoma, anti-PD-1, ~120 with RNA-seq): dbGaP **phs000452**. Both papers' supplements include processed TPM, which is usually enough for a classifier. Apply only if you want uniform reprocessing from raw.
- **Miao 2018** (ccRCC), **Snyder 2017** (urothelial), **Nathanson 2017** (melanoma, anti-CTLA-4): dbGaP. Some processed data is in the supplements or cBioPortal.
- **Atezolizumab NSCLC trials OAK/POPLAR** (Patil 2022, Cancer Cell): EGA, roughly 900 patients. This is the largest NSCLC resource, but access goes through a Roche data access committee.
- **JAVELIN Renal 101** (Motzer 2020, avelumab + axitinib) and **IMmotion150/151** (ccRCC, atezolizumab ± bevacizumab): EGA, controlled.
- **Ravi 2023 SU2C-MARK** (NSCLC, ~150 with RNA-seq): raw data is controlled; check the supplement and GitHub for processed matrices (verify).

dbGaP typically takes 4–8 weeks and needs an institutional signing official. EGA committees vary a lot, and industry-trial data is the slowest.

## Already-harmonised collections (fastest start)

- **CRI iAtlas, ICI module** (iatlas.org; data on Synapse): harmonised expression and response for about a dozen cohorts. It covers many of the ones above, including some controlled cohorts in processed form.
- **TIGER** (tiger.canceromics.org): bulk and single-cell ICI cohorts with response labels.
- **TIDE** (tide.dfci.harvard.edu): processed ICI cohorts used to benchmark TIDE.
- **ICBatlas** and **CAMOIP**: similar portals.
- **Litchfield 2021 (Cell, "CPI1000+")**: a meta-analysis with processed data on Zenodo, covering about 1,000 patients across 12 cohorts (RNA-seq for a subset).

These save a lot of work. Still, I'd re-derive at least the response labels and sample selection from the original papers, because harmonisation choices differ between portals.

## Pitfalls for cross-study validation

1. **Use pre-treatment samples only.** Riaz, Gide and others mix pre- and on-treatment samples in the same series.
2. **Response definitions differ.** Some studies use RECIST CR/PR vs SD/PD. Others use "clinical benefit", which can count SD lasting at least 6 months, and Van Allen and Liu use their own definitions. Pick one rule and reapply it to every cohort where the data allows. Decide explicitly where stable disease goes.
3. **Prior treatment.** Riaz splits patients by prior ipilimumab, and Gide mixes monotherapy with combination therapy. Treat these as covariates or analyse them as separate strata.
4. **Overlapping patients.** Aggregators and meta-analyses can include the same patients under different IDs. Most published response signatures, such as TIDE and IMPRES, were also built or tuned on exactly these cohorts. A truly held-out validation set is harder to find than it looks, so record which cohorts each comparator signature has already seen.
5. **Batch and platform effects.** Studies differ in poly-A vs capture library prep, FFPE vs fresh-frozen tissue, and processing (FPKM vs TPM vs counts). Rank-based or within-sample features hold up better across studies than z-scores across samples. Leave-one-cohort-out validation is the honest test.
6. **Imbalance by cancer type.** Melanoma dominates the open data. IMvigor210 is about 3× bigger than any other single cohort, so weight or stratify for it, or it will drive your model.

## Suggested starting set

Today you can download IMvigor210, Gide, Riaz, Hugo, Kim and Braun, plus the Liu and Van Allen supplementary TPMs. That gives you roughly 750 patients across 4 cancer types, which is enough for leave-one-cohort-out validation with no data access applications. File the dbGaP request for phs000452 and an EGA request for OAK/POPLAR now if you want raw data or a large NSCLC test set later.

I can also write a script that pulls the open cohorts, harmonises gene IDs and response labels, and runs a leave-one-cohort-out setup.

**Harmonised compendia** save a lot of reprocessing:
- **ORCESTRA / PredictIO** (Bareche et al. 2022): uniformly processed ICB datasets as downloadable objects. This is probably the fastest start for cross-study validation.
- **CRI iAtlas, ICI module** (data on Synapse): harmonised expression and response for roughly 10+ cohorts.
- **TIGER** (tiger.canceromics.org) and **TIDE** (tide.dfci.harvard.edu): processed ICB cohorts you can download.
- **Litchfield 2021 (CPI1000+, Cell)**: a reprocessed meta-cohort. It's mostly the same studies listed here, so don't count it as independent validation.

## Apply first (controlled access)

| Cohort | Cancer / drug | Repository |
|---|---|---|
| Van Allen 2015 | Melanoma, ipilimumab (anti-CTLA-4), ~40 with RNA | dbGaP **phs000452** |
| Liu 2019 (Nat Med) | Melanoma, anti-PD-1, ~120 | dbGaP **phs000452** (processed matrices may be in the supplement, check) |
| Miao 2018 | ccRCC, anti-PD-(L)1 | dbGaP |
| McDermott 2018 (IMmotion150), Motzer 2020 (IMmotion151 / JAVELIN Renal 101) | RCC, atezolizumab/avelumab plus VEGF inhibitors | EGA |
| Patil 2022 (POPLAR/OAK) | NSCLC, atezolizumab, several hundred | EGA |
| Ravi 2023 (SU2C-MARK) | NSCLC, anti-PD-(L)1, ~150 | dbGaP (some processed data in the supplement) |

dbGaP approval usually takes weeks to a few months and needs an institutional signing official. EGA requests go to each study's own Data Access Committee, and pharma trial DACs can be slow or restrictive.

## Things that will bite a cross-study classifier
1. **Inconsistent labels.** Studies define "response" differently: CR/PR vs the rest, clinical benefit including durable stable disease (Van Allen), or survival only. Pick one definition, re-derive it from each study's supplementary clinical data, and report it per cohort.
2. **Timepoint leakage.** Several cohorts mix pre- and on-treatment biopsies, so filter to baseline samples explicitly.
3. **Duplicate patients.** The compendia (iAtlas, TIDE, Litchfield, PredictIO) repackage the same patients. Pick "independent" test cohorts by original study, not by portal.
4. **Batch and platform effects.** Data arrives as FPKM, TPM, counts or microarray, with poly-A or capture libraries. 5. **Confounders.** Prior ipilimumab, MSI or EBV status, and combination arms (anti-PD-1 plus anti-CTLA-4, or ICB plus VEGF inhibitors) all shift response rates. Stratify by them or adjust for them.
6. **Benchmarks.** Compare against simple baselines like TMB, CD274 expression, IFN-γ/T-cell-inflamed signatures and TIDE. Reviewers will ask for them.

**Suggested start:** download IMvigor210, Braun 2020, Riaz, Gide and Hugo now, and pull the ORCESTRA/PredictIO versions to cross-check your processing. Submit the dbGaP request for phs000452 (Van Allen and Liu) at the same time, since it's the slowest step and would give you an independent anti-CTLA-4 cohort.

| Ravi 2023 (SU2C-MARK) | NSCLC, anti-PD-(L)1, ~150 | dbGaP (some processed data in the supplement) |

dbGaP approval usually takes weeks to a few months and needs an institutional signing official. EGA requests go to each study's own Data Access Committee, and pharma trial DACs can be slow or restrictive.

## Things that will bite a cross-study classifier
1. **Inconsistent labels.** Studies define "response" differently: CR/PR vs the rest, clinical benefit including durable stable disease (Van Allen), or survival only. Pick one definition, re-derive it from each study's supplementary clinical data, and report it per cohort.
2. **Timepoint leakage.** Several cohorts mix pre- and on-treatment biopsies, so filter to baseline samples explicitly.
3. **Duplicate patients.** The compendia (iAtlas, TIDE, Litchfield, PredictIO) repackage the same patients. Pick "independent" test cohorts by original study, not by portal.
4. **Batch and platform effects.** Data arrives as FPKM, TPM, counts or microarray, with poly-A or capture libraries. Rank-based or within-sample features (e.g. gene-pair or ssGSEA scores) usually transfer across studies better than z-scored expression. Leave-one-study-out cross-validation is the honest evaluation.
5. **Confounders.** Prior ipilimumab, MSI or EBV status, and combination arms (anti-PD-1 plus anti-CTLA-4, or ICB plus VEGF inhibitors) all shift response rates. Stratify by them or adjust for them.
6. **Benchmarks.** Compare against simple baselines like TMB, CD274 expression, IFN-γ/T-cell-inflamed signatures and TIDE. Reviewers will ask for them.

**Suggested start:** download IMvigor210, Braun 2020, Riaz, Gide and Hugo now, and pull the ORCESTRA/PredictIO versions to cross-check your processing. Submit the dbGaP request for phs000452 (Van Allen and Liu) at the same time, since it's the slowest step and would give you an independent anti-CTLA-4 cohort.

I wrote this from memory and didn't check the links in this session, so confirm each accession on GEO, ENA or EGA before you build a pipeline around it.

## 1. Download now (open access)

| Cohort | Cancer / drug | ~n with pre-treatment RNA | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Hugo 2016** (Cell) | Melanoma, anti-PD-1 | ~27 | GEO **GSE78220** (FPKM; raw on SRA) |
| **Riaz 2017** (Cell, CheckMate 038) | Melanoma, nivolumab; some patients had already progressed on ipilimumab | ~50 pre, plus on-treatment | GEO **GSE91061** |
| **Gide 2019** (Cancer Cell) | Melanoma, anti-PD-1 ± anti-CTLA-4 | ~90 | ENA **PRJEB23709** (FASTQ) |
| **Auslander 2018** (Nat Med) | Melanoma, anti-PD-1 / anti-CTLA-4 | ~37 | GEO **GSE115821** |
| **Kim 2018** (Nat Med) | Gastric, pembrolizumab | ~45 | ENA **PRJEB25780** |
| **IMvigor210** (Mariathasan 2018, Nature) | Urothelial, atezolizumab | ~350 (the largest open cohort) | R package **IMvigor210CoreBiologies** (counts and RECIST). Raw data is in EGA (controlled). |
| **Braun 2020** (Nat Med, CheckMate 009/010/025) | ccRCC, nivolumab (everolimus control arm) | ~180 on nivolumab | Processed expression and clinical data in the paper's supplementary tables. Raw data is controlled. |
| **Rose 2021** | Urothelial, anti-PD-1/PD-L1 | ~90 | GEO **GSE176307** |
| **Jung 2019** / **Cho 2020** | NSCLC, anti-PD-1/PD-L1 | ~27 / ~16 | GEO **GSE135222** / **GSE126044** |

GBM response is not RECIST-based, so I'd treat Zhao 2019 as a stress test rather than a core cohort.

## 2. Apply first (controlled access)

- **Van Allen 2015** (melanoma, anti-CTLA-4, n≈42) and **Liu 2019** (melanoma, anti-PD-1, n≈120): both are under dbGaP **phs000452**. Processed matrices are in the paper supplements and on cBioPortal, so you may not need the raw data.
- **Miao 2018** (ccRCC, n≈33): dbGaP **phs001493**.
- **IMmotion150** (McDermott 2018, RCC, atezolizumab ± bevacizumab): EGA **EGAS00001002928**.
- **JAVELIN Renal 101**, **IMmotion151**, **POPLAR/OAK**: these are trial-sponsor datasets. Access goes through EGA data access committees or sponsor platforms such as Vivli or YODA.
- **Ravi 2023** (NSCLC, SU2C-MARK, n≈150 RNA) and the **CPI1000+ compendium** (Litchfield 2021): raw data is controlled. Check the supplements for processed data.

dbGaP approval usually takes 4–8 weeks and needs your institution's signing official. EGA timelines depend on each committee.

## 3. Curated collections (fastest way to start)

These sites have already harmonised many of the cohorts above, with response labels attached:
- **ORCESTRA / PredictIO** (Haibe-Kains lab): ICB cohorts packaged as R MultiAssayExperiment objects. This is the best fit for cross-study validation.
- **CRI iAtlas ICI module**: harmonised ICB cohorts on Synapse. Downloading needs a free Synapse account.

- **Van Allen 2015** (melanoma, anti-CTLA-4, n≈42) and **Liu 2019** (melanoma, anti-PD-1, n≈120): both are under dbGaP **phs000452**. Processed matrices are in the paper supplements and on cBioPortal, so you may not need the raw data.
- **Miao 2018** (ccRCC, n≈33): dbGaP **phs001493**.
- **IMmotion150** (McDermott 2018, RCC, atezolizumab ± bevacizumab): EGA **EGAS00001002928**.
- **JAVELIN Renal 101**, **IMmotion151**, **POPLAR/OAK**: these are trial-sponsor datasets. Access goes through EGA data access committees or sponsor platforms such as Vivli or YODA.
- **Ravi 2023** (NSCLC, SU2C-MARK, n≈150 RNA) and the **CPI1000+ compendium** (Litchfield 2021): raw data is controlled. Check the supplements for processed data.

dbGaP approval usually takes 4–8 weeks and needs your institution's signing official. EGA timelines depend on each committee.

## 3. Curated collections (fastest way to start)

These sites have already harmonised many of the cohorts above, with response labels attached:
- **ORCESTRA / PredictIO** (Haibe-Kains lab): ICB cohorts packaged as R MultiAssayExperiment objects. This is the best fit for cross-study validation.
- **CRI iAtlas ICI module**: harmonised ICB cohorts on Synapse. Downloading needs a free Synapse account.
- **TIGER** (tiger.canceromics.org) and **TIDE** (tide.dfci.harvard.edu): processed expression with response labels.

## Things that can quietly bias cross-study validation

1. **Response definitions differ between studies.** Hugo used irRECIST, Van Allen used clinical benefit, and Riaz kept stable disease as a separate group. Decide whether stable disease counts as a responder, and apply that rule the same way in every cohort.
2. **Some samples were taken after treatment started.** Riaz and Gide include on-treatment biopsies, so filter to pre-treatment samples explicitly.
3. **Prior treatment and combination therapy vary.** Riaz has ipilimumab-progressed patients and Gide includes combination therapy. Stratify on these or report them.
4. **The same patients can appear twice.** Patients may show up in both the curated collections and the original deposits, and the DFCI melanoma cohorts may share patients. Deduplicate before you treat two datasets as independent.
5. **Expression units and pipelines differ.** Studies ship FPKM, TPM or counts from different pipelines. Where you can, reprocess from FASTQ with one pipeline: Gide, Kim, Hugo and Riaz all have raw data. Otherwise, use rank-based or within-sample features so the model stays robust across batches.

A good holdout is leaving out a whole cancer type, for example training on melanoma and testing on IMvigor210 and Braun. Reviewers will ask for it.

Prompt

I'm a bioinformatics postdoc building a classifier that predicts response to immune checkpoint inhibitors (anti-PD-1/PD-L1 or anti-CTLA-4) from pre-treatment tumour RNA-seq. I need cohorts of patients who actually received checkpoint inhibitors, with bulk expression data and a recorded clinical response (RECIST or clinical benefit), ideally several independent cohorts so I can validate across studies. Any cancer type is fine. Where can I get these, and which ones can I download right away versus having to apply for?

For English report generation, you can start today with **ReXGradient-160K** (Hugging Face, click-through agreement). **MIMIC-CXR** is the benchmark reviewers will expect you to use, and its credentialing takes about 1–3 weeks, so apply now. For the non-English experiment, **PadChest-GR** (Spanish + English) and **CASIA-CXR** (French) are the realistic choices. I checked everything on 2026-11-12.

## What I assumed you need
- **R1 (must):** the radiologist's original free-text report for each study, not extracted labels.
- **R2 (preferred):** English, with one non-English set for a second experiment.
- **R3 (preferred):** at least ~10k studies for the main training set.
- **R4 (must):** an academic researcher can get it. I assumed non-commercial use is fine.

## Shortlist
| # | Dataset | Access | Licence | Size | Fit | Checked |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | MIMIC-CXR v2.1.0 | PhysioNet credentialing + CITI training + DUA, ~1–3 weeks | PhysioNet Credentialed Health DUA 1.5.0 | 227k studies / 377k images | strong | today |
| 2 | ReXGradient-160K | HF login + accept agreement, minutes | non-commercial DUA | 160k studies / 273k images | strong | today |
| 3 | CheXpert Plus | free Stanford AIMI account + research use agreement, ~days | Stanford research use, non-commercial | 187k studies / 223k pairs | strong | web search (portal can't be read by script) |
| 4 | IU X-ray (Open-i) | direct download, minutes | CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 | 3,955 reports / 7,470 images | partial (small) | web search (Open-i FAQ) |
| 5 | Naija-CXR (Nigeria) | direct download, minutes | Zenodo lists CC BY 4.0, but the description says non-commercial only | 389 MB zip | partial | today |
| 6 | CASIA-CXR (French) | sample open; full set needs a request form + hand-signed DUA, ~weeks | custom, academic | not checked | partial (non-English) | today |
| 7 | PadChest (Spanish) | request form, ~days | from memory CC BY-SA 4.0, not confirmed | 160k images / 67k patients | partial | papers/GitHub (site down) |
| 8 | PadChest-GR (Spanish + English) | request form, ~days | not confirmed | 4,555 studies | partial | papers (site down) |

## Details
**1. MIMIC-CXR** – https://physionet.org/content/mimic-cxr/2.1.0/
- **Contents:** the full original reports from Beth Israel Deaconess, Boston. This is the default benchmark (RadGraph F1, RadCliQ, ReXrank all report on it).
- **Steps:**
  1. Create a PhysioNet account.
  2. Apply for credentialed access.
  3. Complete CITI "Data or Specimens Only Research" training and upload the certificate.
  4. Sign the DUA on the project page.
- **DUA terms (quoted from the page today):** you will "not share the data", make "no attempt to reidentify individuals", and publications "will also make the relevant code available."
- **Practical notes:**
  - Use the MIMIC-CXR-JPG images (same credentials) with the reports from this project.
  - Don't send reports to online LLM APIs without checking PhysioNet's rules on that.
  - The derived sets (MS-CXR, Chest ImaGenome, CXR-PRO, ReXErr, RadGraph, REFLACX) come with the same terms.

**2. ReXGradient-160K** – https://huggingface.co/datasets/rajpurkarlab/ReXGradient-160K
- **Contents:** 3 US health systems, 79 sites. Reports are split into Indication / Comparison / Findings / Impression (sections were pulled out of the original reports with GPT-4o). Splits are 140k / 10k / 10k, plus a private test set used by ReXrank.
- **Terms:** "non-commercial research and non-clinical purposes only", no redistribution.
- **Caveats:** PNGs are downsampled to 25% of original size, and the download is ~156 GB.
- **Paper:** arXiv [2505.00228](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.00228).

**3. CheXpert Plus** – [AIMI page](https://aimi.stanford.edu/datasets/chexpert-plus), [paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2405.19538)
- **Contents:** Stanford reports split into up to 11 sections, plus demographics, CheXbert labels and RadGraph annotations.
- **Terms:** non-commercial, no redistribution. I didn't read the exact agreement text.
- **Paper using it:** a small multimodal findings-generation model trained on 697k image-text pairs ([Nat Commun 2025](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-58344-x)).

**4. IU X-ray** – https://openi.nlm.nih.gov/faq
- **Contents:** XML reports with Findings and Impression sections.
- **Caveats:** small and heavily de-identified ("XXXX" tokens). NoDerivatives licence.
- **Use:** the standard secondary benchmark. Use the official Open-i download, not the Kaggle or HF mirrors.

**5. Naija-CXR** – https://zenodo.org/records/21781842
- **Contents:** "frontal chest X-ray images paired with expert radiologist annotations and diagnostic reports", released Aug 2026.
- **Not checked:** report length, language and study count. Look inside the zip first.
- **Use:** good as an out-of-distribution test set. Treat it as non-commercial.

**6. CASIA-CXR (French)** – https://www.casia-cxr.net/
- **Contents:** original French reports from several hospitals, covering only 5 findings.
- **Steps:** download the ~80 MB sample to inspect, then submit the full-dataset request form and sign the DUA by hand.
- **Key restriction:** "You may not translate the radiographic reports… without prior written permission." That rules out translate-to-English experiments unless the authors agree.

**7–8. PadChest / PadChest-GR (Spanish)** – https://bimcv.cipf.es/bimcv-projects/padchest/ and https://bimcv.cipf.es/bimcv-projects/padchest-gr/
- **PadChest:** the largest non-English set. The report excerpts are heavily preprocessed (stop-words and affixes removed), so they are poor targets for fluent text generation.
- **PadChest-GR:** has sentence-level grounded reports in Spanish and English, with bounding boxes. This makes it the better choice for your secondary experiment. The English text is translated from the Spanish originals. Paper: [NEJM AI 2025](https://doi.org/10.1056/aidbp2401120).
- **Access:** both need an access request, and you agree not to share the data or try to re-identify anyone. The BIMCV site returned HTTP 503 today, so these terms come from the papers and the authors' GitHub.

## Known, not confirmed
- **BIMCV-COVID19+ (Spanish):** from memory, it includes Spanish radiology reports alongside CXR/CT. I couldn't check because the BIMCV site was down.
- **CANDID (the larger New Zealand set, 22k reports):** it is probably under the same restriction that closed CANDID-PTX, but I didn't check.

## Not recommended, and why
- **MIMIC-CXR-JPG:** images and labels only. The reports are in MIMIC-CXR.
- **BRAX (Brazil):** the page says "Free-text reports are not yet provided in the current version."
- **CANDID-PTX:** has English reports, but since Feb 2024 it isn't available outside Health New Zealand ([DigitalNZ](https://digitalnz.org/records/45567577)).
- **CheXpert (original), NIH ChestX-ray14, VinDr-CXR:** labels or boxes only, no reports.
- **FMCEB-CXR (Nigeria):** a 42 KB file of labels only, no images or report text.

## What I could not find
- No public CXR + report set in German, Japanese, Korean or Chinese. Chinese sets such as CX-CHR appear to be private.
- [PARROT](https://github.com/mk-runner/Awesome-Radiology-Report-Generation) is multilingual, but I believe it is reports without images; I didn't check.

## Next step
Apply for MIMIC-CXR credentials and the PadChest-GR request today, since both take time. Meanwhile, download ReXGradient-160K and IU X-ray and build your pipeline on them.

I've also made an interactive version of the shortlist with filters and an export of the access steps: `/private/tmp/e-za8iiV/home/cwd/dataset-shortlist.html`

Sources: [PadChest-GR arXiv](https://arxiv.org/html/2411.05085), [CASIA-CXR paper](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0925231224012499), [CASIA-CXR downloads](https://casia-cxr.net/downloads.html), [Awesome-RRG list](https://github.com/mk-runner/Awesome-Radiology-Report-Generation), [ReXGradient paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.00228), [CANDID-PTX Figshare](https://auckland.figshare.com/articles/dataset/CANDID-PTX/14173982), [CANDID-PTX RSNA](https://pubs.rsna.org/doi/10.1148/ryai.2021210136), [CheXpert Plus arXiv](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2405.19538), [CheXpert Plus AIMI](https://aimi.stanford.edu/datasets/chexpert-plus), [PadChest arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.07441), [PadChest GitHub](https://github.com/auriml/Rx-thorax-automatic-captioning), [Open-i FAQ](https://openi.nlm.nih.gov/faq), [RRG review](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2405.10842)

## Details
**1. MIMIC-CXR** – https://physionet.org/content/mimic-cxr/2.1.0/
- **Contents:** the full original reports from Beth Israel Deaconess, Boston. This is the default benchmark (RadGraph F1, RadCliQ, ReXrank all report on it).
- **Steps:**
  1. Create a PhysioNet account.
  2. Apply for credentialed access.
  3. Complete CITI "Data or Specimens Only Research" training and upload the certificate.
  4. Sign the DUA on the project page.
- **DUA terms (quoted from the page today):** you will "not share the data", make "no attempt to reidentify individuals", and publications "will also make the relevant code available."
- **Practical notes:**
  - Use the MIMIC-CXR-JPG images (same credentials) with the reports from this project.
  - Don't send reports to online LLM APIs without checking PhysioNet's rules on that.
  - The derived sets (MS-CXR, Chest ImaGenome, CXR-PRO, ReXErr, RadGraph, REFLACX) come with the same terms.

**2. ReXGradient-160K** – https://huggingface.co/datasets/rajpurkarlab/ReXGradient-160K
- **Contents:** 3 US health systems, 79 sites. Reports are split into Indication / Comparison / Findings / Impression (sections were pulled out of the original reports with GPT-4o). Splits are 140k / 10k / 10k, plus a private test set used by ReXrank.
- **Terms:** "non-commercial research and non-clinical purposes only", no redistribution.
- **Caveats:** PNGs are downsampled to 25% of original size, and the download is ~156 GB.
- **Paper:** arXiv [2505.00228](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.00228).

**3. CheXpert Plus** – [AIMI page](https://aimi.stanford.edu/datasets/chexpert-plus), [paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2405.19538)
- **Contents:** Stanford reports split into up to 11 sections, plus demographics, CheXbert labels and RadGraph annotations.
- **Terms:** non-commercial, no redistribution. I didn't read the exact agreement text.
- **Paper using it:** a small multimodal findings-generation model trained on 697k image-text pairs ([Nat Commun 2025](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-58344-x)).

**4. IU X-ray** – https://openi.nlm.nih.gov/faq
- **Contents:** XML reports with Findings and Impression sections.
- **Caveats:** small and heavily de-identified ("XXXX" tokens). NoDerivatives licence.
- **Use:** the standard secondary benchmark. Use the official Open-i download, not the Kaggle or HF mirrors.

**5. Naija-CXR** – https://zenodo.org/records/21781842
- **Contents:** "frontal chest X-ray images paired with expert radiologist annotations and diagnostic reports", released Aug 2026.
- **Not checked:** report length, language and study count. Look inside the zip first.
- **Use:** good as an out-of-distribution test set. Treat it as non-commercial.

**6. CASIA-CXR (French)** – https://www.casia-cxr.net/
- **Contents:** original French reports from several hospitals, covering only 5 findings.
- **Steps:** download the ~80 MB sample to inspect, then submit the full-dataset request form and sign the DUA by hand.
- **Key restriction:** "You may not translate the radiographic reports… without prior written permission." That rules out translate-to-English experiments unless the authors agree.

**7–8. PadChest / PadChest-GR (Spanish)** – https://bimcv.cipf.es/bimcv-projects/padchest/ and https://bimcv.cipf.es/bimcv-projects/padchest-gr/
- **PadChest:** the largest non-English set. The report excerpts are heavily preprocessed (stop-words and affixes removed), so they are poor targets for fluent text generation.
- **PadChest-GR:** has sentence-level grounded reports in Spanish and English, with bounding boxes. This makes it the better choice for your secondary experiment. The English text is translated from the Spanish originals. Paper: [NEJM AI 2025](https://doi.org/10.1056/aidbp2401120).
- **Access:** both need an access request, and you agree not to share the data or try to re-identify anyone. The BIMCV site returned HTTP 503 today, so these terms come from the papers and the authors' GitHub.

## Known, not confirmed
- **BIMCV-COVID19+ (Spanish):** from memory, it includes Spanish radiology reports alongside CXR/CT. I couldn't check because the BIMCV site was down.
- **CANDID (the larger New Zealand set, 22k reports):** it is probably under the same restriction that closed CANDID-PTX, but I didn't check.

## Not recommended, and why
- **MIMIC-CXR-JPG:** images and labels only. The reports are in MIMIC-CXR.
- **BRAX (Brazil):** the page says "Free-text reports are not yet provided in the current version."

- **CheXpert (original), NIH ChestX-ray14, VinDr-CXR:** labels or boxes only, no reports.
- **FMCEB-CXR (Nigeria):** a 42 KB file of labels only, no images or report text.

## What I could not find
- No public CXR + report set in German, Japanese, Korean or Chinese. Chinese sets such as CX-CHR appear to be private.
- [PARROT](https://github.com/mk-runner/Awesome-Radiology-Report-Generation) is multilingual, but I believe it is reports without images; I didn't check.

## Details
**1. MIMIC-CXR** – https://physionet.org/content/mimic-cxr/2.1.0/
- **Contents:** the full original reports from Beth Israel Deaconess, Boston. This is the default benchmark (RadGraph F1, RadCliQ, ReXrank all report on it).
- **Steps:**
  1. Create a PhysioNet account.
  2. Apply for credentialed access.
  3. Complete CITI "Data or Specimens Only Research" training and upload the certificate.
  4. Sign the DUA on the project page.
- **DUA terms (quoted from the page today):** you will "not share the data", make "no attempt to reidentify individuals", and publications "will also make the relevant code available."
- **Practical notes:**
  - Use the MIMIC-CXR-JPG images (same credentials) with the reports from this project.
  - Don't send reports to online LLM APIs without checking PhysioNet's rules on that.
  - The derived sets (MS-CXR, Chest ImaGenome, CXR-PRO, ReXErr, RadGraph, REFLACX) come with the same terms.

**2. ReXGradient-160K** – https://huggingface.co/datasets/rajpurkarlab/ReXGradient-160K
- **Contents:** 3 US health systems, 79 sites. Reports are split into Indication / Comparison / Findings / Impression (sections were pulled out of the original reports with GPT-4o). Splits are 140k / 10k / 10k, plus a private test set used by ReXrank.
- **Terms:** "non-commercial research and non-clinical purposes only", no redistribution.
- **Caveats:** PNGs are downsampled to 25% of original size, and the download is ~156 GB.
- **Paper:** arXiv [2505.00228](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.00228).

**3. CheXpert Plus** – [AIMI page](https://aimi.stanford.edu/datasets/chexpert-plus), [paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2405.19538)
- **Contents:** Stanford reports split into up to 11 sections, plus demographics, CheXbert labels and RadGraph annotations.
- **Terms:** non-commercial, no redistribution. I didn't read the exact agreement text.
- **Paper using it:** a small multimodal findings-generation model trained on 697k image-text pairs ([Nat Commun 2025](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-58344-x)).

**4. IU X-ray** – https://openi.nlm.nih.gov/faq
- **Contents:** XML reports with Findings and Impression sections.
- **Caveats:** small and heavily de-identified ("XXXX" tokens). NoDerivatives licence.
- **Use:** the standard secondary benchmark. Use the official Open-i download, not the Kaggle or HF mirrors.

**5. Naija-CXR** – https://zenodo.org/records/21781842
- **Contents:** "frontal chest X-ray images paired with expert radiologist annotations and diagnostic reports", released Aug 2026.
- **Not checked:** report length, language and study count. Look inside the zip first.
- **Use:** good as an out-of-distribution test set. Treat it as non-commercial.

**6. CASIA-CXR (French)** – https://www.casia-cxr.net/
- **Contents:** original French reports from several hospitals, covering only 5 findings.
- **Steps:** download the ~80 MB sample to inspect, then submit the full-dataset request form and sign the DUA by hand.
- **Key restriction:** "You may not translate the radiographic reports… without prior written permission." That rules out translate-to-English experiments unless the authors agree.

**7–8. PadChest / PadChest-GR (Spanish)** – https://bimcv.cipf.es/bimcv-projects/padchest/ and https://bimcv.cipf.es/bimcv-projects/padchest-gr/
- **PadChest:** the largest non-English set. The report excerpts are heavily preprocessed (stop-words and affixes removed), so they are poor targets for fluent text generation.
- **PadChest-GR:** has sentence-level grounded reports in Spanish and English, with bounding boxes. This makes it the better choice for your secondary experiment. The English text is translated from the Spanish originals. Paper: [NEJM AI 2025](https://doi.org/10.1056/aidbp2401120).
- **Access:** both need an access request, and you agree not to share the data or try to re-identify anyone. The BIMCV site returned HTTP 503 today, so these terms come from the papers and the authors' GitHub.

## Known, not confirmed
- **BIMCV-COVID19+ (Spanish):** from memory, it includes Spanish radiology reports alongside CXR/CT. I couldn't check because the BIMCV site was down.
- **CANDID (the larger New Zealand set, 22k reports):** it is probably under the same restriction that closed CANDID-PTX, but I didn't check.

## Not recommended, and why
- **MIMIC-CXR-JPG:** images and labels only. The reports are in MIMIC-CXR.
- **BRAX (Brazil):** the page says "Free-text reports are not yet provided in the current version."
- **CANDID-PTX:** has English reports, but since Feb 2024 it isn't available outside Health New Zealand ([DigitalNZ](https://digitalnz.org/records/45567577)).
- **CheXpert (original), NIH ChestX-ray14, VinDr-CXR:** labels or boxes only, no reports.
- **FMCEB-CXR (Nigeria):** a 42 KB file of labels only, no images or report text.

## What I could not find
- No public CXR + report set in German, Japanese, Korean or Chinese. Chinese sets such as CX-CHR appear to be private.
- [PARROT](https://github.com/mk-runner/Awesome-Radiology-Report-Generation) is multilingual, but I believe it is reports without images; I didn't check.

## Next step
Apply for MIMIC-CXR credentials and the PadChest-GR request today, since both take time. Meanwhile, download ReXGradient-160K and IU X-ray and build your pipeline on them.

## Details
**1. MIMIC-CXR**: https://physionet.org/content/mimic-cxr/2.1.0/
- **Contents:** images from Beth Israel Deaconess in Boston, each study with its full report (findings and impression sections). It is the main benchmark in this field.
- **Access:** create a PhysioNet account → apply for credentialing (ID check and a reference) → complete the CITI "Data or Specimens Only Research" course → sign the agreement on the project page.
- **Agreement terms** (quoted on the page): no sharing, no attempt to re-identify, and "any publication which makes use of the data will also make the relevant code available."
- **Images:** MIMIC-CXR-JPG has JPGs and labels but no reports. Most papers use its images with the MIMIC-CXR reports; the same credential covers both.
- **Watch out:** PhysioNet's rules forbid sending this data to third-party online LLM services, so use local models or an approved cloud setup. Reports often refer to earlier exams; CXR-PRO on PhysioNet is a cleaned version with those references removed.
- **Paper using it:** "Evaluating progress in automatic chest X-ray radiology report generation" (Patterns 2023, [10.1016/j.patter.2023.100802](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.patter.2023.100802)), which introduced the RadGraph F1 and RadCliQ metrics.

**2. CheXpert Plus**: https://aimi.stanford.edu/datasets/chexpert-plus
- **Contents:** Stanford Hospital reports, each split into 11 sections, with images as DICOM and PNG.
- **Access:** follow "Download here" to Redivis, log in, accept the agreement, then download the `df_chexpert_plus` CSV (the reports) and the images.
- **Terms:** search results quoting the agreement say research use only, no commercial use, no redistribution. I couldn't confirm whether Redivis approves requests automatically or by hand.
- **Why use it:** it is a second large English hospital, which makes it a good check of how well a MIMIC-trained model transfers.

**3. ReXGradient-160K**: https://huggingface.co/datasets/rajpurkarlab/ReXGradient-160K
- **Contents:** reports with Indication, Comparison, Findings and Impression sections. Official train/validation/test splits are 140k/10k/10k, and a further 10k private test set backs the ReXrank leaderboard.
- **Access:** log in to Hugging Face and accept the agreement; this is the fastest way to get large-scale English data.
- **Limits:** non-commercial and non-clinical use only, no redistribution. Images are PNGs shrunk to 25% of original size.

**4. IU X-ray / Open-i** (openi.nlm.nih.gov)
- **Contents:** findings and impression text with frontal and lateral images. You can start on it today; it's commonly used as a second test set.
- **Check:** the site is a JavaScript app the tool couldn't read, so the download link and the CC BY-NC-ND licence are from memory. Confirm them in a browser and use the NLM original rather than Hugging Face copies.

**5–6. PadChest and PadChest-GR** (BIMCV, Spain): bimcv.cipf.es/bimcv-projects/padchest/ and /padchest-gr/
- **PadChest:** Spanish reports from Hospital San Juan, about 1 TB. **Caveat:** the released report text was heavily normalised for anonymisation (case, accents and stop-words removed), so it isn't natural prose.
- **PadChest-GR:** reports written by radiologists in both Spanish and English, with a box for each finding. It is the cleanest bilingual option ([NEJM AI 2025](https://doi.org/10.1056/aidbp2401120)), but the reports were curated for the dataset rather than taken from clinical practice.
- **Access:** the BIMCV site returned errors (HTTP 503) today, so the request-form process comes from secondary sources ([arXiv 1901.07441](https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.07441), [authors' GitHub](https://github.com/auriml/Rx-thorax-automatic-captioning)).

**7. CASIA-CXR (French)**: https://www.casia-cxr.net/
- **Contents:** narrative reports "originally written in French" ([Neurocomputing 2024](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neucom.2024.128478)).
- **Access:** an ~80 MB sample is downloadable now; the full set needs a request form and a use agreement.
- **Unknowns:** the site gives no total size and names no licence.

**8. REFLACX**: https://physionet.org/content/reflacx-xray-localization/1.0.0/
- Reports dictated by radiologists while their eye movements were tracked, on MIMIC-CXR images. Useful as a supplement, not on its own.

**9. BIMCV-COVID19+**: Spanish reports, COVID-positive patients only, available by request under BIMCV's research use agreement. Its population is narrow.

**10. Naija-CXR**: https://zenodo.org/records/21781842
- A new (2026) Nigerian dataset whose contents list "free radiologist reports." Report coverage and image count aren't stated.
- The record says CC BY 4.0, but its description limits use to non-commercial research, so treat it as non-commercial.

## Known, not confirmed
- **IU X-ray:** the licence and download page are from memory.
- **PadChest family:** the exact terms are unconfirmed because the BIMCV site was down. Check both before you plan around them.

## Not recommended, and why
- **MIMIC-CXR-JPG, original CheXpert, NIH ChestX-ray14, VinDr-CXR:** labels or boxes only, no report text.
- **BRAX (Brazil):** labels taken from Portuguese reports; the report text isn't released (from memory).
- **CANDID-PTX (New Zealand):** has 19,237 X-rays with free-text reports, but since 2024 it is closed to anyone outside Health New Zealand (figshare record, version 2).
- **FMCEB-CXR:** 5,517 Nigerian reports, but I couldn't confirm it includes the images.
- **MIMIC add-ons (CXR-PRO, RadGraph, ReXErr, etc.):** processed versions of MIMIC-CXR, not new image–report sources.

## What I could not find
- An English set bigger than IU X-ray that you can download with no sign-up or agreement.
- Report sets in German, Chinese, Japanese or Korean weren't searched in depth.

## Next step
Start PhysioNet credentialing now, since it takes the longest. While it runs, you can be working within the hour: accept the ReXGradient-160K agreement and download the IU X-ray set. For the secondary experiment, submit a PadChest-GR request: being bilingual, it gives you a direct English vs. Spanish comparison. Request full PadChest as well if you want scale.

The interactive shortlist is at `/private/tmp/e-kZvH16/home/cwd/dataset-shortlist.html`.

Sources: [CheXpert Plus paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2405.19538), [AIMI data](https://aimi.stanford.edu/data), [CANDID-PTX figshare](https://auckland.figshare.com/articles/dataset/CANDID-PTX/14173982), [CASIA-CXR OpenReview](https://openreview.net/forum?id=4tj6oWXDGo), [BIMCV-COVID19 datos.gob.es](https://datos.gob.es/es/catalogo/pudat0002-bimcv-covid-19-un-gran-conjunto-de-datos-anotados-de-imagenes-de-rx-y-tc-de-pacientes-con-covid-19), [BIMCV-COVID19 arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.01174), [PadChest-GR arXiv](https://arxiv.org/html/2411.05085v1)
